Completing your IR35 questionnaire

You have been asked to complete a short questionnaire so the end-hirer can determine your IR35 (off-payroll) status for an assignment. Allow about fifteen minutes.

Why you are doing this

Your answers, alongside the hirer's, feed a Status Determination Statement (SDS) — the formal decision on whether your engagement sits inside or outside IR35. The hirer makes the final determination; your job is to describe how you actually work, accurately.

Nothing can be decided until you have answered. No determination is made and no statement is issued until your questionnaire is in.

1Signing in

  1. You will receive an email invitation from IR35 Workbench Team (assessments@ir35workbench.co.uk). Open the link in it. If it is not in your inbox, check your junk folder.
  2. Choose a password for your account — at least 8 characters. You are not asked to set up an authenticator app.
  3. After that, sign in at https://ir35workbench.co.uk/orsted/ whenever you need to, in whichever way suits you:
    • A six-digit code by email — type your email address, click Email me a sign-in code, then enter the code. Nothing to remember.
    • Your password — click Use a password instead.

The invitation link signs you in as you, so please don't forward it to anyone else.

2Before you start — have these to hand

  • Your contract for this assignment (with the agency or the client).
  • How you work in practice: substitution rights, who directs your work, how, where and when you work, how you are paid, and what equipment you use.

3Completing the questionnaire

  1. Sign in and open My IR35 status, then Open my questionnaire.
  2. If an assessment fee applies, you are asked to pay it before the questionnaire opens: £75 + VAT (£90.00), or £65 + VAT (£78.00) if you are logging in to be reassessed for a second or third time. Pay by bank is recommended; card and Revolut Pay are also accepted. Payment is taken securely by Revolut, and the questionnaire opens as soon as it is confirmed. If you want the invoice in your company's name, add your company details before you pay. Your VAT invoice is emailed to you and can be downloaded at any time from My IR35 status.
  3. Answer each question about this specific engagement and how you actually work.
  4. Most questions are three-way (for example: yes / it depends / no). Choose the one that best reflects reality.
  5. If you are unsure what a question means, click Guidance under it for a short explanation.
  6. Click + Notes / evidence (optional) under a question to add a sentence of context — especially for anything that isn't clear-cut. This is useful evidence.
  7. Submit when you are done. If something about the assignment changes later, you can go back in and update your answers; they are re-merged and re-audited.
What a question looks like
8Does the client have the right to direct the consultant regarding their day-to-day working methods?
ⓘ Guidance ⌃ 1
This is about the way the work is done rather than what is delivered, and does not include having to follow industry standards or regulations.
No — consultant decides their own methods 2
Partly / in some respects
Yes — the client directs the methods
+ Notes / evidence (optional) 3
  1. 1Guidance — click it to open a short explanation of what the question means. Click again to close it.
  2. 2Your answer — click the one that fits. The chosen answer turns light green. Green only means “selected”; it does not mean the answer points inside or outside IR35.
  3. 3+ Notes / evidence (optional) — click it to open a notes box and write a sentence of evidence: what the contract says, or what actually happens. If a note is already there, the box is open with it showing.

4What the questions cover

  • Substitution — could someone else do the work in your place, and who would arrange and pay them?
  • Control — who decides how, when and where the work is done?
  • Mutuality of obligation — is there any obligation to offer and accept ongoing work, or is it tied to a defined project?
  • Business on your own account — do you work for other clients, carry costs or financial risk, use your own equipment, and put right defective work at your own cost?

5What happens next

  • Your answers combine with the hirer's assessment and the determination runs.
  • If the picture is clear, an SDS is produced. If it is borderline, a qualified specialist reviews it before any decision is made.
  • You will be able to see your SDS from My IR35 status once it is issued.
  • If you disagree with the determination you can make representations to the end-hirer, who will respond within 45 days.
